title: What can this test detect?
hook: Match a traffic budget to an approximate detectable lift.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: with your traffic, what's the smallest change you can reliably see?

misconception: Treating minimum detectable effect as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: with your traffic, what's the smallest change you can reliably see?
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: A fixed design uses baseline .5, 80% power, and 100 observations per arm. Using MDE=(1.96+.84)√(.5/n), what approximate absolute lift can it detect?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-minimum-detectable-effect/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: At baseline.5 and80%power, normal approximation MDE=(1.96+.84)*sqrt(.5/n), n per arm. n=100→19.799%,400→9.899%,1600→4.950%. Explain approximation and fixed design, not guarantee.

src/demos/probability/p100-minimum-detectable-effect/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: At baseline.5 and80%power, normal approximation MDE=(1.96+.84)*sqrt(.5/n), n per arm. n=100→19.799%,400→9.899%,1600→4.950%. Explain approximation and fixed design, not guarantee.

claims.text: The retained approximations are 19.799 points at 100 per arm and 9.899 at 400 per arm. Quadrupling sample size halves this design’s minimum detectable effect.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-minimum-detectable-effect/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: At baseline.5 and80%power, normal approximation MDE=(1.96+.84)*sqrt(.5/n), n per arm. n=100→19.799%,400→9.899%,1600→4.950%. Explain approximation and fixed design, not guarantee.

claims.text: This normal approximation fixes the baseline, significance threshold and target power. An MDE describes the design’s detection probability under a specified effect, not a guarantee that any one experiment will detect it.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-minimum-detectable-effect/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: At baseline.5 and80%power, normal approximation MDE=(1.96+.84)*sqrt(.5/n), n per arm. n=100→19.799%,400→9.899%,1600→4.950%. Explain approximation and fixed design, not guarantee.

claims.text: Under the same approximation, halving MDE requires sample size to do what? MDE scales with 1/√n, so reducing it by two requires four times as many observations.
